prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System supports wildfire detection/suppression amid dry fuels, steep terrain, variable winds, lightning, human ignitions, and wildland-urban exposure.

Elements:
• Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): staffed portal presenting information, recommendations, and status to authorized personnel.
• North Lookout Camera Mast: northern-rim coverage of drainages, roads, ignition corridors; sends Thermal Spot Snippet after local processing identifies candidate heat signature.
• South Lookout Camera Mast: opposing viewshed with terrain-obscured overlapping coverage. Both masts have hardened power distribution, equipment cabinets, lightning protection, seasonal-maintenance access; video reaches operations network via licensed wireless, with cellular degraded-mode backup where available.
• Horizon Ridge Drone Dock; Drone Tasking Service: directed aerial observation for inconclusive/blocked views and scene updates.
• Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine; Smoke Classifier Module: screen imagery/observations; advisory, not authoritative.
• MesoWest Weather Fusion Node: localized weather context for spread, aviation, exposure, timing.
• VHF Radio Gateway Repeater: digital/field-radio continuity beyond broadband.
• Crewline Mobile Tablet: mobile access to approved operational information.
• Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console; East Retardant Loading Pump; West Retardant Loading Pump: mission-demand/loading/tempo context for Tanker Base Manager.

Actors: local fire agencies, county emergency management, state wildland fire resources, aviation support units, cooperating public safety partners; County Emergency Liaison (warnings/roads/shelters/emergency integration); Duty Detection Officer (Orion: reviews cues, requests verification, recommends escalation; Confirmed Ignition State only with supporting observations/procedures); Air Attack Supervisor (advises tactics); Helitack Crew Leader; Drone Pilot Operator (shared conditions/timing/hazards awareness).

Detection: observation→screening→review→confidence/location/context presentation→authorized acceptance/rejection/further verification under agency procedure. Suppression supports initial-attack priorities, resource movement/updates, aviation coordination, fire assessment, safety pauses, and Airspace Restricted State recognition under incident rules. Command remains with incident command; only timely information, procedural support, traceable recommendations, coordination aids. No autonomous dispatch, independent command, or direct control of aircraft, vehicles, pumps, cameras, drones, crews.

New part:
S031: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is referred to by the site engineering alias Kestrel in drawings and maintenance records for this deployment.
S032: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock is located on a graded pad near the central ridge road so that launch, recovery, charging, and shelter functions remain accessible to maintenance personnel.
S033: The dock includes weather-rated enclosures, charging interfaces, local health monitoring, and a secure network termination for coordination with the rest of the support system.
S034: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock produces the Battery Swap Ticket when its maintenance controller records that a flight battery has reached the configured replacement threshold.
S035: Drone Tasking Service manages approved unmanned flight requests, records mission constraints, and presents task status without acting as an independent authority for flight release.
S036: The Drone Pilot Operator uses Drone Tasking Service to review proposed routes, current dock status, and operational constraints before coordinating any field action through established procedures.
S037: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine is referred to by the site engineering alias Lantern in architecture diagrams and configuration work orders.
S038: Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine aggregates camera detections, weather inputs, geospatial context, and operator feedback into traceable recommendations for fire detection and suppression support.
S039: Smoke Classifier Module runs as a bounded analytics component that scores visual observations for plume likelihood and passes confidence values to the broader analytics workflow.
S040: The analytics services retain event timing, source identifiers, model version information, and operator acknowledgments so that later review can reconstruct how a recommendation was presented.
S041: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node is referred to by the site engineering alias Brindle in network inventory and integration test records.
S042: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node ingests station observations, forecast grids, and configured quality checks to provide a consistent weather picture for the operating area.
S043: MesoWest Weather Fusion Node sends the Wind Shift Bulletin when its configured weather rules identify a significant change in local wind behavior.
S044: VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides a monitored bridge between selected radio traffic and operator workstations, with recording and access controls aligned to incident policy.
S045: Caldera Incident Command Portal is the primary operator interface for the Duty Detection Officer, County Emergency Liaison, and other command staff who need consolidated situational information.
S046: The portal displays camera views, detection history, weather context, map layers, and status transitions such as Confirmed Ignition State and Airspace Restricted State.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
